title: Transport and Commuting
subtitle: Buses, trains, bikes and the journey to school or work

parts.title: Notices and messages
parts.instructions: For each notice, choose what it means.
notices: NORTHLINE BUSES: From Monday, the number 14 will stop at the hospital instead of the market. Buses run every twenty minutes until 11 p.m.
TRAINS TO COASTON: Because of track repairs, buses will replace trains between Millbrook and Coaston on Sunday. Please allow an extra thirty minutes.
JAN: Running late! The bus has broken down at the bridge. Please start without me and save me a seat. I should be there by ten past.
CITY BIKE HIRE: The first thirty minutes are free. After that, it costs £1 for each extra half hour. Return the bike to any station.
TAXI RANK: Please queue here and do not stand in the road. Cash and cards accepted. After midnight, fares are double.

questions.prompt: What will change on Monday?

Buses will start to run later at night.
The number 14 bus will stop somewhere new.
questions.explanation: The 14 will stop at the hospital instead of the market.

options: Buy a new ticket at the station
Allow more time for the journey
Take a different train in the morning
questions.explanation: Buses replace the trains on Sunday, so passengers should allow an extra thirty minutes.

questions.prompt: What does Jan say in her message?
options: She will arrive after the others have started.
She has already taken a seat.
She will go home by bus.
questions.explanation: She asks them to start without her, and says she will be there by ten past.

Short trips do not cost anything.

parts.title: Choosing how to travel
parts.instructions: Read what each person is looking for. Match each person to the best text. There are three extra texts.

people.text: Anselma wants to travel across the country at the lowest possible price. She does not mind if the journey takes a long time.
Bartolo has a flight at six in the morning and needs a quick and reliable way to get to the airport very early.
Clothilde would like to explore the countryside by bike, so she needs a train that allows her to take her bicycle.
Dag is visiting a city for a day and wants one ticket that lets him use all the buses and trams as often as he likes.
Emilia would like to go to an island and enjoy the sea views on a slow and relaxed trip.

texts.title: Scooter Hire

texts.title: Budget Coach

texts.title: Sprint Airport Shuttle

parts.title: My long journey to school
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
For the last two years, I have travelled to school by train and bus. The journey is ninety minutes each way, and I leave home at ten past six in the morning, when it is still dark in winter. My friends cannot believe it, but I have found ways to make the time pass.

On the train, I do my homework, or I read. In the first year, I tried to sleep, but the seats were too hard, and I always woke up with a sore neck. Now I bring a small cushion in my bag. I also listen to podcasts about history and science, which means that I am sometimes better prepared for my lessons than students who live next to the school.

The part that I dislike most is the bus. It is always full, and in the rain, the windows are so wet that I cannot see anything. Last winter, the bus broke down twice in one week, and we had to wait in the cold for forty minutes. Since then, I always carry a flask of hot chocolate.

However, there are good things about my journey, too. Every morning I see the same people, and over time we have become friends. One of them, an old man called Mr Tate, teaches me to play chess on a small board that he brings. He says I am improving, but he always wins. I do not mind. I think that I would miss my long journey if it ever ended.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about the early morning?
options: She often misses the first train.
She arrives at school an hour early.
She leaves home before it is light in winter.
questions.explanation: She leaves at ten past six, when it is still dark in winter.

questions.prompt: Why did she stop trying to sleep on the train?
options: She was afraid to miss her stop.
questions.explanation: The seats were too hard and she woke up with a sore neck.

questions.prompt: What does she like about listening to podcasts?
options: They help her to forget the wet weather.
They help her to fall asleep.
They make her more ready for lessons.
questions.explanation: She is sometimes better prepared for her lessons than the students who live next to the school.

questions.prompt: Why does she take a flask of hot chocolate?
options: She gets very hungry in the afternoon.
Her bus once broke down and she had to wait.
The bus is always too hot.
questions.explanation: The bus broke down twice in one week and they waited forty minutes in the cold.

questions.prompt: How does the writer feel about her journey now?
options: She is tired of her friends.
She is bored with Mr Tate.
She wants to move closer to school.
She would be sad if it stopped.
questions.explanation: She says that she thinks she would miss her long journey if it ended.

parts.title: A city without traffic jams
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Ten years ago, the city of Greenhaven had a big problem. Every morning, thousands of cars filled the centre, the air was dirty, and a short journey could take an hour. [1] They decided to do something about it, and the result surprised everybody.

First, they built new bicycle lanes that are separated from the traffic. [2] Many parents, who had been afraid to let their children ride on the road, changed their minds.

Next, the council made the bus service cheaper and faster. A single ticket now costs half the old price. [3] The queue for the bus at rush hour has doubled, but the buses now come every five minutes.

Not everybody was pleased at the beginning. Some shop owners said that customers would not come without cars. [4] In fact, the number of visitors has gone up by 20 per cent, because the centre is now quieter and more pleasant.

Today, nearly half of the people in Greenhaven go to work by bike, bus or on foot. [5] Visitors from other cities often come to find out how it was done.
sentences: These lanes made cycling feel much safer.
The old railway station is now a museum.
As a result, more people left their cars at home.
Many other cities are now planning to follow the same path.
Bus drivers there are now paid more than before.
This was a fair worry, but it was not true.
Their solution was simple but brave.
A taxi in Greenhaven costs twice as much as in other cities.

gaps.explanation: "Every morning, thousands of cars filled the centre" describes the problem; "They decided to do something" follows the idea of a simple but brave solution.
New bicycle lanes are mentioned; sentence C says they made cycling feel safer, and the next sentence says parents changed their minds.
The bus service became cheaper, so more people left their cars at home; the next sentence mentions longer queues.
Shop owners worried that customers would not come, and "In fact" shows that this worry was not true.
Nearly half of the people now go to work by bike, bus or foot; other cities want to follow, and visitors come to learn how.

parts.title: Travelling by train
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Travelling by train is one of the most comfortable ways to see a country. You can sit back, watch the view and [1] a book without worrying about traffic. However, a good journey needs some planning. It is usually [2] to buy your ticket in advance, because prices rise as the day of travel gets closer. Remember to check the time of your train and the platform number, which is often [3] on the screens only a few minutes before departure. On busy routes, it is wise to [4] a seat, especially at weekends. If you have a lot of luggage, arrive early, [5] the platform can be crowded. Finally, keep your ticket in a safe place until the end of the journey, because staff may [6] to see it at any time.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: On a train you can sit and read a book.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: Buying in advance is cheaper because prices rise closer to the day of travel.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: The platform number is shown on screens a few minutes before the train leaves.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: On busy routes it is wise to book a seat in advance.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "Because" gives the reason for arriving early: the platform can be crowded.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: Staff may ask to see your ticket at any time.

parts.title: An email about a journey
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Hi Marlon,
I hope you had a good journey home! Mine was long [1] very interesting. The train was forty minutes late, [2] I missed the bus in Dalton and had to wait for the next one. I sat next to a man [3] told me stories about his life as a train driver. I did not mind the delay [4] all, because he was so funny. I got home at midnight, and my mother was waiting [5] me at the station. Next time, I am going to take the earlier train, [6] I can arrive before dark.
Take care,
Selma

gaps.explanation: "But" shows a contrast: the journey was long but interesting.
"So" gives the result: the train was late, so she missed the bus.
The relative pronoun refers to the man: a man who told me stories.
"Not at all" is the fixed expression.
"Waiting for" someone is the correct phrase.
"So (that) I can arrive before dark" expresses the purpose.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: anatolia
turns.text: Good afternoon, passengers waiting for the number twelve to the museum. The board shows half past three, but that is the old timetable, so please ignore it. Because of roadworks in the town centre, the normal bus is running late today. It will not leave until four o’clock, I’m afraid. However, we have organised a special minibus which will go earlier, at a quarter to four. It will stop in front of the café, next to the ticket machine. If you prefer to wait for the normal bus, you may, but it will be very full. Thank you for your patience, and we apologise for the delay.

question.prompt: What time does the first bus to the museum leave?
question.explanation: The board’s half past three is the old timetable and the normal bus leaves at four, but the special minibus goes at a quarter to four.

turns.speaker: clarimond
turns.text: Hello. I’d like a ticket to Oxford, please. I’m coming back on Sunday evening.

turns.speaker: dunstan
turns.text: A single is twelve pounds. A day pass is eighteen, but it’s only for people who come back the same day.

turns.speaker: clarimond
turns.text: I thought about the day pass, but I’m staying two nights at my sister’s.

turns.speaker: dunstan
turns.text: Then I’d get the kind where you pay for both journeys together. It’s twenty pounds, so it’s cheaper than two singles.

turns.speaker: clarimond
turns.text: I nearly bought a single online last night, but I decided to wait. Actually, yes, I’ll take the same as my sister bought last time. She said it was good value.

turns.speaker: dunstan
turns.text: Lovely. That’s twenty pounds, please.

question.prompt: Which ticket will the woman buy?
question.explanation: The day pass is only for the same day and she nearly bought a single, but she wants the ticket that pays for both journeys together.

turns.speaker: fenella
turns.text: Excuse me, which platform is the train to Bristol? My ticket says platform seven.

turns.speaker: evaristo
turns.text: That was changed this morning. Seven is for the London trains today. Let me check the screen. Oh, it says platform five.

turns.speaker: fenella
turns.text: Five? OK, I’ll go over the bridge.

turns.speaker: evaristo
turns.text: Wait, wait. Sorry, that’s the delayed train from Cardiff. The Bristol one has been moved to the platform next to it, so it’s four.

turns.speaker: fenella
turns.text: I’m so glad I asked.

turns.speaker: evaristo
turns.text: Yes, there’s a short walk, so hurry up. It leaves in six minutes.

turns.speaker: fenella
turns.text: Thank you. You’ve saved my day.

question.prompt: Which platform does the woman need?
question.explanation: Seven is only on her ticket and five is the delayed Cardiff train; the man corrects himself and says that the Bristol train is on four.

turns.speaker: hyacinth
turns.text: I’m thinking of taking the coach to Manchester next weekend instead of the train.

turns.speaker: gawain2
turns.text: Really? The coach takes almost five hours. The train takes two.

turns.speaker: hyacinth
turns.text: I know, so it isn’t about saving time.

turns.speaker: gawain2
turns.text: Is it the seats? I heard the new coaches are very comfortable.

turns.speaker: hyacinth
turns.text: Maybe, but I always sleep badly on them. Actually, I looked at the prices yesterday. The train ticket is sixty pounds, and the coach is only fifteen.

turns.speaker: gawain2
turns.text: Wow, that’s a big difference.

turns.speaker: hyacinth
turns.text: Yes. I’m a student, so every pound counts. I can use the money for a nice dinner there.

turns.speaker: gawain2
turns.text: Sensible. Take a good book!

question.prompt: Why does the woman think of taking the coach?
question.explanation: She says it is not about time and she sleeps badly on coaches, but the coach ticket is fifteen pounds against sixty for the train.

turns.speaker: ignatius2
turns.text: Hi Juliette, it’s Ignace. About tomorrow: I know you usually take the green line to get to the airport, but it’s closed for repairs all weekend, so forget that. Some people say there’s a direct bus from the airport station, but it only runs on weekdays. So this is what you do. Take the blue line from your house and stay on it for eight stops. Don’t get out earlier, even if the map looks easier. Change at the big station in the middle of town, the one with the clock tower. The airport train leaves from platform two there. Call me if you get lost. See you tomorrow! Bye.

question.explanation: The green line is closed and the direct bus runs only on weekdays, so she must change at the big station with the clock tower in the middle of town.

turns.speaker: leocadie
turns.text: Hello, Mr Evans, it’s Tom’s mum. I’m calling about why Tom was late today. I know it’s the third time this term, but this morning was different. He didn’t oversleep and he didn’t miss the bus either. In fact, he got up at half past six, before me. He usually goes by bike, but when he went into the garage, the back wheel was completely flat. I suggested the bus, but he said the next one wasn’t for forty minutes, so he walked all the way. It took him an hour. I’m sorry. He did his best. Please call me if you want to talk.

question.prompt: Why was Tom late for school?
options: His bike had a flat tyre.
question.explanation: He got up early and refused the bus, but his bike wheel was flat, so he had to walk.

turns.speaker: mercutia
turns.text: Hi Nik, it’s Mercutia. I’m calling about Saturday’s concert. I was going to drive, but the car park next to the hall is always full, and I’d have to pay a lot. I nearly booked a taxi, but then I saw it costs more than the ticket! So I’ll use the tram in the end. The stop is only five minutes from my flat, and it leaves you right outside the main door of the hall. It runs until midnight, so I won’t have a problem coming home. Tell me if you want to join me. Bye!

question.prompt: How will Mercutia go to the concert?
question.explanation: She was going to drive and nearly booked a taxi, but she rejects both and says she will take the tram that stops outside the hall.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: orestes
turns.text: Excuse me, I think you’re in my seat. It’s number forty-two, by the window.

turns.speaker: perdita2
turns.text: Oh, is it? My ticket says forty-two as well. Look.

turns.speaker: orestes
turns.text: That’s for tomorrow’s train, though. Today is the fourth.

turns.speaker: perdita2
turns.text: Oh no, you’re right. I’m so sorry. I was sure I had the right day. I’ll move.

turns.speaker: orestes
turns.text: It’s all right. I’m not angry about the train being late, we’ve waited for twenty minutes, it’s quite normal. I just want to sit down after a long day. And I haven’t lost my ticket, don’t worry, I have it here.

turns.speaker: perdita2
turns.text: Of course, let me take my bag. Sorry again!

question.prompt: Why is the man a little annoyed?
options: Another passenger has taken his seat.
question.explanation: He says the lateness is normal and he has his ticket, but he wants to sit in his own seat, which she has taken by mistake.

turns.speaker: quintilian
turns.text: So how do we get to Edinburgh on Friday? I’m checking flights.

turns.speaker: rosaline
turns.text: Flying is quick, but the airport is far, and the prices go up before holidays. What about the night bus?

turns.speaker: quintilian
turns.text: I tried that once. I couldn’t sleep, and I felt terrible all day. No way.

turns.speaker: rosaline
turns.text: OK. Then the train in the morning. But if it’s late, we’ll miss the lunch with Dad.

turns.speaker: quintilian
turns.text: Exactly. We’d better take the early one, at seven. Then we have plenty of time.

turns.speaker: rosaline
turns.text: Fine, I’ll set the alarm. It’s early, but it’s better than rushing.

question.prompt: What do the speakers agree about?
options: They should take the night bus.
They should catch an early train.
question.explanation: Flights are expensive and far, and the night bus is rejected, so both agree on the seven o’clock train to be safe for lunch.

turns.speaker: theodora
turns.text: You’ve stopped driving to work, haven’t you?

turns.speaker: sempronius
turns.text: Yes, about two months ago. I thought the train would be more expensive, but it’s about the same with petrol and parking. And to be honest it’s late quite often.

turns.speaker: theodora
turns.text: So why do you do it?

turns.speaker: sempronius
turns.text: Well, in the car I’m just staring at the road for an hour. Now I open my laptop and answer emails, so I’m ready when I arrive. I even finished a report last week.

turns.speaker: theodora
turns.text: That sounds useful.

turns.speaker: sempronius
turns.text: It is. My boss was surprised, because I leave the office earlier now.

question.prompt: Why does the man like going to work by train?
options: He can get some work done.
It costs much less than driving.
It nearly always arrives on time.
question.explanation: The cost is similar and the train is often late, but he uses the hour to answer emails and write a report.

turns.speaker: ulpian
turns.text: Did you hear that buses won’t run tomorrow? There’s a strike.

turns.speaker: valeria
turns.text: Yes, I read it this morning. I was a bit irritated at first, because it takes me an hour to walk to the office.

turns.speaker: ulpian
turns.text: So will you go?

turns.speaker: valeria
turns.text: My boss said I can stay at home, which is nice, but that isn’t what I’m thinking about. These drivers work long hours, and their pay hasn’t gone up for three years. If I were them, I’d do the same.

turns.speaker: ulpian
turns.text: That’s true. They have a hard job.

turns.speaker: valeria
turns.text: Exactly. I’ll just walk, it’s only one day. Good for my health.

question.prompt: How does the woman feel about the bus strike?
question.explanation: She was irritated at first and could stay at home, but she says that the drivers have long hours and low pay and she would do the same.

turns.speaker: xanthe
turns.text: Are you ready for Saturday? The ferry leaves at nine.

turns.speaker: wulfric
turns.text: I’m trying to be, though I was ill the last time I took a boat. I decided to take a tablet this time, so I won’t worry. The weather forecast is good too.

turns.speaker: xanthe
turns.text: And the ticket is only eight pounds each, not bad for an hour at sea.

turns.speaker: wulfric
turns.text: Not bad at all. I haven’t slept well this week, I keep thinking about the seals we might see! I’ve wanted to visit the island since I was a kid.

turns.speaker: xanthe
turns.text: You sound like a child.

turns.speaker: wulfric
turns.text: I feel like one!

question.prompt: How does the man feel about the trip to the island?
question.explanation: He has solved the sea sickness and the price is fine, and he cannot sleep because he wants to see the seals and has wanted to visit the island since he was a kid.

turns.speaker: zephyrin
turns.text: Is that your new bike? It looks heavy.

turns.speaker: ysabel
turns.text: It is a bit, because of the battery. I thought I’d hate it, but I take it up the stairs only once, and I leave it in the garage.

turns.speaker: zephyrin
turns.text: It must have cost a fortune.

turns.speaker: ysabel
turns.text: Almost six hundred pounds, which I couldn’t believe at first. But I’ve stopped using the bus, and I don’t pay for petrol any more. In three months I’ll have paid for it.

turns.speaker: zephyrin
turns.text: Is it safe in the rain?

turns.speaker: ysabel
turns.text: Yes, I feel fine. The lights are great. Honestly, it’s the best decision I’ve made this year, it was worth every penny.

question.prompt: What does the woman think of her new bike?
options: It is too heavy to carry.
It is dangerous in the rain.
question.explanation: The weight is not a problem and it feels safe, and although it was expensive she saves money and calls it her best decision.

parts.title: Information at a station
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Westbury Station. This is travel information for passengers. Because of an accident on the line, the nine fifteen train to Cardiff is delayed. The company first told us it would be twenty minutes late, and then half an hour, but the latest news is that it will be forty minutes behind time. We are very sorry about this. The train will not leave from platform four, as it says on the board, because that platform is closed for cleaning. It will use platform six instead, which you reach from the stairs at the end of the hall. If you do not want to wait, the company has organised replacement buses. They leave from the car park, behind the station, not from the bus station in front. Please follow the yellow signs, and ask the staff in the orange jackets if you need help. The buses will go every fifteen minutes, and they are free for anyone with a train ticket. Now some news about the facilities. The café on platform two is closed for repairs. The owners hoped to open it today, but some problems were found with the kitchen, so it will probably open next week. For hot drinks, there is a coffee machine near the ticket office; it takes coins and cards, but not notes. There is another one outside, by the taxi stand, but it is out of order. Finally, a reminder for people who have lost something. If you left a bag or an umbrella on a train, don’t go to the ticket office. Please go to the information desk, in the main hall, next to the shop. It is open from seven in the morning until eight at night. Remember to bring something that shows your name, and to describe the object clearly. Thank you for your patience, and we hope you have a pleasant journey.

gaps.prompt: The train that normally leaves at 9.15 will be late by ___ minutes
gaps.explanation: The company said twenty and then thirty minutes, but the latest news is forty.

gaps.prompt: The delayed Cardiff train will go from platform ___
gaps.explanation: Platform four is closed for cleaning, so it uses platform six.

gaps.prompt: Replacement buses wait in the ___ park
gaps.explanation: The buses leave from the car park behind the station, not from the bus station in front.

gaps.prompt: The café on platform two is shut because of ___
gaps.explanation: The owners hoped to open it today but it is closed for repairs.

gaps.prompt: Hot drinks are sold from a coffee ___ near the ticket office
gaps.explanation: The machine near the ticket office works; the one outside is out of order.

gaps.prompt: Passengers who lost an umbrella should go to the ___ desk
gaps.explanation: Not the ticket office: they should go to the information desk in the main hall.

parts.title: An interview with a bus driver
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Barnard, thank you for coming. Most people choose a job like yours because they love driving. Is that why you became a bus driver?

turns.speaker: barnard
turns.text: Not really. My father drove a bus for thirty years, but I always said I’d never do the same. And I’m not a big fan of cars, to be honest. I worked in an office for ten years doing the same thing every day, and I was bored out of my mind. One day I saw an advert for drivers and I thought, why not? I needed a change, and it was the best decision I’ve ever made.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: You start very early. Who gets on first?

turns.speaker: barnard
turns.text: My first bus leaves at ten past five. You’d think tourists would be early, but they get up late. Students and shoppers appear later too, around eight or nine. At that hour it’s the nurses, cleaners and builders, people who start work before most of us are awake. I know many of them by name now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What’s the hardest part of the job?

turns.speaker: barnard
turns.text: Well, people think the passengers are hard, but most are very friendly. Cold weather is not nice, especially in winter when the doors freeze, but you get used to it. For me it’s the traffic. When there are roadworks, and it takes two hours to move a mile, you can’t relax, and the passengers get angry with you even though it’s not your fault.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I’ve heard something unusual happened on your bus once.

turns.speaker: barnard
turns.text: Yes! A famous footballer travelled on my bus once, but that was no big deal, he was very quiet. And I’ve never lost a child, thankfully. But a few years ago a woman started to feel pains on the number nine, and a little later she had her baby, right at the back of the bus! Two passengers helped her until the ambulance arrived.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How did you feel about all that?

turns.speaker: barnard
turns.text: People expect me to be proud, but at the time I was honestly terrified. I wasn’t embarrassed, there was no time to be, I just drove as fast as I safely could to the hospital. Afterwards, I was shaking for an hour. Now it’s a good story, and they sent me a card every year!

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How have buses changed since you started?

turns.speaker: barnard
turns.text: They’re not slower, in fact, the new ones are quicker because the lanes are separate. Tickets are not much dearer either, you pay about the same. The big change is the engine. Many of the newer ones have an electric motor. They’re quiet, there’s no smell, and the air in the city is cleaner.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Finally, what advice would you give to someone who wants to do your job?

turns.speaker: barnard
turns.text: Stay calm and be patient, with everyone, the traffic and yourself. Don’t try to drive fast, you can’t change a late bus, and speed causes accidents. And you don’t need to repair buses, the mechanics do that. Just smile and say good morning, people remember it.
